Benny was not the biggest bear in the forest, nor the fastest, nor the strongest, but he was the kindest. His fur was soft and brown. His eyes were warm and round, and his paws were as gentle as falling leaves. Every evening, when the sun began to sink behind the hills, Benny would wander slowly back to his favorite spot beneath the tallest pine tree. It was there on a bed of moss and grass that he liked to curl up and watch the stars appear one by one. The forest at dusk was a magical place. The sky shifted from gold to pink, from pink to purple, and finally to the deep velvet of night. Fireflies blinked like tiny lanterns. Cripps began their steady song. The air grew cooler, carrying the scent of pine needles and wild flowers. Benny loved this time of day. It was the forest's bedtime, and he always felt calm and safe as the world grew quieter. But on this particular evening, something unusual happened. Benny stretched his arms wide, rubbed his sleepy eyes, and opened his mouth to yawn. Oh, and what a yawn it was. It wasn't just an ordinary yawn. It was a big round rolling yawn that seemed to travel farther than any yawn had ever gone before. The sound drifted through the trees like a soft breeze. It floated over the river, across the meadow, and up into the branches of the tallest oaks. The rabbits who were nibbling clover near their burrow twitched their noses.
